Why write this post？

This course is renowned for its high quality, but it is also notably challenging and requires considerable effort to understand and finish. I treat this course as a project for both an introduction to databases and C++. The purpose is to familiarize myself with C++ syntax and database principles. Most of the knowledge is difficult but beneficial for me. I will use many posts under the tag ‘cs15445’ to document my notes on completing this course, focusing mainly on the thought process during project implementation and the knowledge acquired.

However, since this is about my personalized thoughts and learning, it will be more like a notebook without a strict, clear structure. It’s primarily for facilitating further contemplation during note-taking and for quick recall in the future.

Task #1 - Copy-On-Write Trie

In this task, we need to modify trie.h and trie.cpp to implement a copy-on-write trie.

What is cow trie?

When I first see the description of this task, I am confused why this task has this weird demand?

“why we just directly add a node or remove a node on or from the original tree?”

The key to understand why we use CoW style is to understand what we can benefit from the CoW style stuffs. So I search on the internet and get the summary as follows. And I underlying two of the most important things.

“Copy on Write (CoW) trie” is a data structure that implements the Copy on Write strategy. This strategy involves creating a copy of a data structure only when a modification is made. If no changes are made, the original data structure is shared among all references to it.

The use of the CoW style in a trie (a tree-like data structure used to store associative data like a dictionary or a phone book) offers several advantages:

  1. Memory Efficiency: CoW trie only duplicates nodes when modifications are necessary, meaning that it uses memory more efficiently compared to always duplicating the entire data structure.
  2. Immutable Snapshots: It allows for the creation of immutable snapshots. When a trie is copied, the new version shares unchanged parts with the original, ensuring that previous versions of the data remain unaltered and accessible.
  3. Concurrency and Safety: This style is beneficial in concurrent programming as it reduces the complexity of managing shared resources. By ensuring that modifications don’t affect other references to the data structure, CoW trie provides a safer environment for multi-threaded operations.
  4. Performance Optimization: In scenarios where reads are more frequent than writes, CoW tries to improve performance by reducing unnecessary duplication.

In summary, a Copy on Write trie is a variation of the standard trie data structure that is optimized for scenarios where immutability, memory efficiency, and safe concurrent access are important. This is achieved by only copying parts of the data structure when modifications are made, rather than copying the entire structure.

General idea to implement Get method

​ This method only takes a string_view as argument, and it will return a const value pointer(note: this value type of this pointer is various, it means this method uses template.)

​ The general idea is to traverse the string_view, if find nullptr or not find, then returns nullptr(means the key-value is not in this trie.). If traverse all the char in this string_view, the node still can be found. We then use dynamic_cast to cast it to ‘const TrieNodeWithValue * ‘, if the result is nullptr, it means the type of the value is mismatched, then the method returns nullptr. If cast successfully, we returns the cast value_.(note this project uses plenty of smart pointers, so we need to use .get() method to get the pointers we needed.)

General idea to implement Put method

​ This method implementation is more difficult than the first one. Since the situations we faced is more diversity. I have two ideas of solving this problem(one is using the traverse method while the other one is using the recursive method). Actually, these two methods can be seen as one. Traverse version is more intuitive, but the implement needs more code. Recursive version like the compiler will help you to complete some details using stack. We here first introduce the recursive version.

  1. Recursive

    First, we need to understand which part of the trie nodes need to be clone, and which part of trie nodes need to be resusing. The answer is, the nodes need to be modified is the clone part and the nodes need not to be modified should be reusing. In other words, when we implement this method, we should traverse the string_view to find the clone words, and the reusing nodes are the left part of this trie.(can simply connected by the children map in the last clone node). Second, we put these clone nodes into a sequential containers(a vector) to record the path. Third, we just link these nodes one by one together(there will be two situations, one is node exists, the other is node does not exists(this need to use nullptr to take a position in the vector(the second step), so u can judge whether situation u faced)). Last we return the trie.
